assignments.evidence: Funerary benediction 'ato mXe ...' asks abundant water for the dead, beside 'at mXe' for bread.
pqr (paqar) is the standard title of the crown prince, found beside qore 'king'.
Verb tk(e) 'love' in royal epithets meaning 'beloved of <god>'.
Recalled as the verb 'offer' in offering contexts; split against are partly by elimination.
Recalled gloss 'cow' (livestock word; xlbi already covers bull); cf. Nubian tii 'cow'.
abr 'man' is the counterpart of kdi 'woman' in Meroitic texts.
mlo 'good' recurs in funerary benedictions (mlo-lo 'it is good').
The 'ato mXe' / 'at mXe' formula: abundant water / abundant bread.
Bare noun ar recalled as 'boy, son'; are carries the verb sense, so partly elimination.
ant is the common priestly title, rendering Egyptian hm-ntr 'prophet'.
lX 'great' qualifies titles and persons (the great/elder one); distinct from mXe 'abundant'.
Inside mkdi 'goddess' (mk + kdi) and kdite 'sister'; opposite abr 'man'.
Ste recalled as 'mother' among kinship terms; the only kin word left once kdi is woman.
Weak recall; takes 'meat, animal' once dime takes cow.
Recalled as the numeral 'two'; no other test word fits a numeral.
Verb are recalled as 'take, receive'; tre takes 'offer'.
